clue.text: Fine bananas by a river up a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate, fine
bananas is slang for mad
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone up a riverside tree is said to be fine and going bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole charade, as this is a down clue; A1 (first-class) is conventionally written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian evergreen grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: Crowd easily whipped up in a second in London borough, start to finish

indicators.note: the second 'in' tells us the short pieces go inside the borough's name
the first letter of the borough moves round to the end

parts.note: Brent is a borough in north-west London
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A mob is stirred up in no time in a London borough, from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the borough's first letter to its end (RENTB), and 'in' puts A plus the second inside; Brent is in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a group of protesters hired or easily gathered to make trouble.

clue.text: Motion, maybe, supported by a character getting notice

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so is supported by, what follows

parts.note: Andrew Motion was Poet Laureate (PL) when the puzzle appeared
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: A debating motion gets backing from an eccentric and attracts attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion is the poet Andrew Motion, UK Poet Laureate 1999-2009, so 'maybe' marks him as an example of a PL.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displayed publicly to announce something.

clue.text: Have a fit fellow shed restraint after eliminating last of flab

indicators.note: eliminating says a letter is struck out of the phrase for shedding restraint

parts.note: to break out is to escape restraint

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word flab

explanation.surface: A man loses his inhibitions after losing some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminating last of flab' removes B from BREAK OUT, leaving REAK OUT after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out is to become wildly agitated or lose control, to throw a fit.

clue.text: A gamble skirting very professional opinion

indicators.note: skirting means the word for gamble runs round the outside of the next piece

parts.note: to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: Taking a risk that sidesteps an expert's view.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance given, such as a lawyer's or doctor's considered view.

clue.text: Prize judge placed above set award?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is set above the second

parts.note: an Emmy is an award for television, the TV set

explanation.surface: A judge sits above a television prize in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' is the verb, as in forcing open with a lever (a variant of prise).
explanation.definitionFit: A jemmy is a short crowbar used to lever or force things open.

clue.text: Bully left woman

parts.note: to haze is to bully or harass, especially newcomers

explanation.surface: A bully abandoned a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Negotiated deals without a cigar in hotel

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letter given as written, removed from the mixture

explanation.surface: A deal was struck without a cigar in a smart hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' says the A comes out: the letters of DEALS and CIGAR, less one A, rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Claridge's is a famous luxury hotel in Mayfair, London.

clue.text: She's regularly among lean birds

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A woman is often seen among thin birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'lean birds' give E, N, I, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, so it can stand for any woman, she.

clue.text: Bell, perhaps, making one abandon drink

indicators.note: abandon says the letter for one leaves the drink

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bell rings when someone gives up their cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Bell is the former BBC reporter and independent MP; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin is a first name, as borne by the journalist and politician Martin Bell.

clue.text: One's enthralled by attractiveness, a magnetic quality?

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the word for attractiveness

parts.note: charm is attractiveness
one is I, and one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: Someone is captivated by an appealing, magnetic personality.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' looks like part of the definition but supplies the last letter; 'enthralled by' puts I'S (one's) inside the attractiveness word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal attraction that draws others in.

clue.text: A model working in publicity gained artistic prize

indicators.note: in says the middle pieces sit inside the letters for publicity

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of model are set going in a new order

explanation.surface: A model working in PR won an arts award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the model into LMEDO; the Cannes prize name means 'golden palm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palme d'Or is the top award at the Cannes film festival.

clue.text: Leg broken by exercises in competition

indicators.note: broken by says the cricket word is split apart with the exercises inside

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, ON
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: An athlete's leg is injured by training during a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An open is a tournament anyone may enter, like the golf Open.

clue.text: Decorative workers fashioned cute cross

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Craftsmen made a sweet cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuccoers apply ornamental plaster to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Nut and hint of brandy put into mixed trifle

indicators.note: put into says one letter goes inside the jumbled pudding
mixed means the letters of trifle are stirred into a new order
hint of takes just the opening letter of brandy

explanation.surface: A recipe: nuts and a dash of brandy go into a stirred trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges the pudding to FILERT, and 'put into' places the brandy's first letter within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is a hazelnut, especially of a cultivated kind.

clue.text: Composer losing his grip around suite's finale

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround another piece
losing, as in losing control, signals the letters run wild
finale takes the last letter of suite

explanation.surface: A composer loses his hold on a suite's closing movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' scrambles HIS GRIP around E, the last letter of 'suite's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottorino Respighi was an Italian composer, known for The Pines of Rome.

clue.text: Extremely strict guide put back forms of public access?

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme, first and last, letters of strict
put back means the word for guide is written backwards

parts.note: to steer is to guide

explanation.surface: Someone strict sends a guide back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives REETS; the question mark flags that streets are a loose, playful sense of access routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets are public roads, routes that give people access.

clue.text: Plea to cool it put at risk

definitions.meaning: a request to stop being angry, as two words: stop the fury

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it asks someone to stop being furious; as one it means to imperil or jeopardise.

clue.text: Inspector screened a couple of grand in baggage?

indicators.note: in says the short pieces go inside the word for baggage

parts.note: baggage is a dated insult for a woman, as is tart
G is a grand, a thousand pounds; two of them give GG

explanation.surface: A customs officer checked a couple of thousand hidden in luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Taggart was a Scottish TV detective series about DCI Jim Taggart; 'screened' hints at TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Taggart is the fictional Glasgow police detective of the long-running TV show.

clue.text: Explanation not good for defeat

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: a gloss is an explanation of a word or text

explanation.surface: An excuse that won't do for losing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a defeat, as in a game lost.

clue.text: Drink taken by sick dramatist

indicators.note: the drink is taken by the sick one, set beside it

parts.note: one is a drink, as in 'a quick one'
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A sick person takes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was an American playwright, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Foreign peer obscuring sun in a search for Roman feature?

indicators.note: obscuring says the peer covers up and replaces the letter for sun

parts.note: a quest is a search
duc is French for duke, a peer

explanation.surface: A foreign nobleman blocks the sun during a search for Roman remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring' makes the French duke stand where the sun's letter was, giving QUEDUCT; a 'foreign' peer is the usual signal for a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqueducts, raised channels carrying water, are typical structures of Roman engineering.

clue.text: Bug limitlessly consuming fruit

indicators.note: consuming says the words eat up, and so contain, the answer

explanation.surface: A bug keeps eating fruit without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'bUG LImitlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid.

clue.text: They have brushes with female team members reversing direction?

indicators.note: reversing direction swaps north for south, so N becomes S

parts.note: oxen are animals yoked in a team

explanation.surface: Women in a team encounter turnabouts.
explanation.walkthrough: N (north) is swapped for S (south) in OXEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's bushy tail is called its brush.

clue.text: Tall Welshman snubbed in Herts town

indicators.note: in says the shortened name goes inside the town

parts.note: Tring is a town in Hertfordshire (Herts), England

indicators.note: snubbed, cut short like a snub nose, drops the final letter

parts.note: Owen is a typical Welsh name

explanation.surface: A tall Welshman is cold-shouldered in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' cuts the Welshman's name short to OWE; Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering means very tall, rising high above.

clue.text: Songwriter producing new number in mostly austere time

indicators.note: in says the new pieces go inside the shortened period
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Lent is the period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A songwriter writes a fresh number during a lean period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the fasting season, leaving LEN, which then holds NNO.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon co-wrote most of the Beatles' songs.

clue.text: Belittle group of activists in audience with leftist rebel

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a cell is a small group of political activists
Clare Short was a left-wing Labour MP who rebelled against her government

explanation.surface: A radical cell speaks before an audience alongside a left-wing rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short resigned from Blair's cabinet over Iraq and was known as a Labour rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell short is to undervalue or disparage someone.

clue.text: Pouring out largely dry wine, ignoring navy rum

indicators.note: pouring out suggests the letters spill out in a new order
largely means most of the word, losing its last letter
ignoring says the letter for navy is left out

explanation.surface: Someone pours out nearly all the dry wine but refuses the navy's rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts DRY to DR and 'ignoring navy' takes N from WINE, leaving WIE; DRWIE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old slang word for odd, strange.
